value.body: A BBA track that applies business subjects to hospitals and health services — hospital operations, healthcare finance and billing, health insurance, medical records, quality and accreditation, and health laws. It prepares you for non-clinical, administrative work; it does not qualify you to treat patients. Some universities offer a similar separate degree, the Bachelor of Hospital Administration (BHA).

items.label: Regulator
items.note: Alongside the affiliating university; BBA, BCA and BMS were brought under AICTE from 2024-25

items.label: BHA students (separate degree)
items.note: All modes; BBA students in this track are counted under BBA

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12 in any stream. Admission is by Class 12 marks, CUET-UG, or a university's own test. Some universities offer the specialisation from the start as a named programme; others let you choose it in the second or third year. Many programmes include a hospital internship.

value.title: At a glance
items: Entry work is in hospital front offices, billing and insurance desks, and patient-services teams; shifts and weekend duty are common.
Hospital-manager posts, especially in government health programmes, usually ask for an MHA, MBA (Healthcare) or MPH.
An internship in a hospital and familiarity with hospital software help in hiring.
Common next steps: an MHA or an MBA in healthcare management.
